notes: The English is Tagore's own translation, The Morning Song of India. It is prose, two paragraphs to a stanza, so it cannot be set line against line.

Romanization: ISO 15919 as a transliteration of the Bengali letters, not of the sung pronunciation: the inherent vowel is written wherever the script has no hasanta (jaẏa, taba; sung roughly 'joy', 'tobo'); ব is b throughout (bidhātā, not vidhātā), as Bengali has no separate v letter; য় is ẏ, য is y, ড় ṛ, ঢ় ṛh, ং ṁ, ঁ m̐, ৃ r̥, ৎ t; conjuncts with ব-phalā are written letter by letter (āhbāna, śaṅkhadhbani, duḥsbapne, rājeśbara). Compounds are one word where the source writes them so, its hyphens kept. The dandas । and ॥ are given as full stops.
Readers who know the anthem's usual Hindi-style romanization ('Jana Gana Mana Adhinayaka Jaya He, Bharata Bhagya Vidhata') will find this one stricter: it writes every letter of the Bengali script.
line 5.2: the source spells 'পূণ্য' (pūṇya) for the usual 'পুণ্য' (puṇya, 'holy'); romanized as written.
line 2.2: 'খৃস্টানী' (khr̥sṭānī), Christians, is the source's spelling; kept as written.
